NoteNlpAccessor::remove_bullets¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::remove_bullets() const

Keep List Items While Removing Their Markers¶

remove_bullets() removes a recognized list marker from the beginning of each line while retaining the item text. It is useful when list membership is presentation detail and the words should become ordinary prose for matching, search, or tokenization.

Leading spaces and tabs may precede a marker. The accepted markers are:

Family

Accepted form

Boundary requirement

Unordered ASCII

-, *, +

Followed by a space, tab, or end of line.

Unordered Unicode

•, ‣, ⁃

Followed by a space, tab, or end of line.

Ordered

One or more ASCII digits followed by . or )

Marker punctuation is followed by a space, tab, or end of line.

The boundary requirement protects ordinary text. -word is not a list item, 3.14 value is not mistaken for item 3, and a line beginning with an unrelated non-ASCII character remains valid UTF-8 text. Marker recognition is performed only at line starts after indentation; a dash in the middle of a sentence is never considered.

If one or more markers are removed, item lines and ordinary lines in that cell are joined by normalized ASCII whitespace. Blank lines disappear as part of that compaction. If the cell contains no recognized marker, it is returned byte-for-byte, including newlines and indentation. Thus the method is a list projection, not an unconditional line joiner.

The result is a newly allocated, shape-identical Text Note. A line containing only a marker contributes no text, and a cell containing only empty marked items becomes an empty string without changing the Note’s shape. Undefined propagates; non-Text dtypes reject.

Example 1: Every Marker Family And Its Boundaries¶

const auto items = pluss::note::make({
    "- alpha\n* beta\n+ gamma\n1. first\n2) second\n"
    "• round\n‣ triangle\n⁃ hyphen\n-word\n3.14 value\nÉclair",
});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(items.nlp().remove_bullets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["alpha beta gamma first second round triangle hyphen -word 3.14 value Éclair"]

Example 2: Unicode Marker Recognition Does Not Need An ASCII Marker¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"• standalone"}).nlp().remove_bullets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["standalone"]

Example 3: Ordinary Multiline Text Is Preserved Exactly¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"First line.\n-word stays"})
        .nlp().remove_bullets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["First line.\n-word stays"]

Example 4: Shape Is Independent Of Line Count¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"Copyright 2026", "a (draft)",
                             "- item", "use `x` now"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    matrix.nlp().remove_bullets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["Copyright 2026", "a (draft)"], 
  ["item", "use `x` now"]
]
